mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown four consecutive weeks of shrinking deficit from baseline (-74.7 to -64.3). This momentum reflects an ongoing reopening trajectory that should persist, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks relative to the last four.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC deficit narrowed each week from -74.7 to -64.3 over the last 4 weeks
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the last 28 days despite the prior 4-week improving streak, falsifying pure momentum continuation.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has fallen steadily from 25.0 to 20.3 over four weeks, indicating households are spending less time at home. Once RESIDENTIAL drops below 20 points above baseline, reduced at-home behavior should translate into higher discretionary retail and recreation visits within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 20 points above baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 25.0 to 20.3 over the last 4 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 2 weeks even after RESIDENTIAL crosses below 20, indicating the behavioral link is absent.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, and PARKS signal a coordinated policy-driven reopening phase where restrictions are being eased across commuting and outdoor activity categories together. This joint easing should compound and lift RETAIL_REC more than any single series would predict alone over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, and PARKS all improve week-on-week simultaneously for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:all three series improved in each of the last 3 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 4 weeks even though WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, and PARKS all continued improving jointly, rejecting the compounding-policy-easing mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: Commute-linked mobility recovery requires both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES to rise together, since transit use without workplace destinations (or vice versa) does not generate incidental retail trips. When both series increase by more than 3 points week-on-week simultaneously, incidental retail and recreation visits along commute routes should rise within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES increase by more than 3 points week-on-week in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -56.4 to -45.4 and TRANSIT rose from -65.7 to -57.7 over 4 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the following 2 weeks despite both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES jointly increasing by more than 3 points in a given week.

mechanism_narrative: The approach of summer (decision point June 15) combined with PARKS mobility steadily improving toward baseline suggests a seasonal shift toward outdoor and adjacent retail activity. This seasonal effect should push RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks as warmer weather encourages more out-of-home trips.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -91.9 to -87.3 over 4 weeks
fact:decision date is mid-June, entering summer season
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next 4 weeks even as PARKS continues improving and the season progresses further into summer.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM improvement decelerated sharply in the most recent week (from +6.4 points week-on-week to +1.2 points), suggesting essential-goods demand is saturating near baseline. When GROCERY_PHARM weekly improvement falls below 2 points, it signals reduced urgency-driven trips, which should coincide with flat RETAIL_REC growth over the following week as overall mobility recovery plateaus temporarily.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly improvement falls below 2 points
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM week-on-week gain slowed from 6.4 to 1.2 points in the most recent week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise strongly over the next week despite GROCERY_PHARM's deceleration below the 2-point threshold.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT improvement decelerated in the latest week (from +4.0 points to +0.7 points week-on-week), which may indicate renewed caution or partial reinstatement of transit-related restrictions. Such deceleration should precede a slowdown or reversal in RETAIL_REC growth within two weeks if policy tightening is underway.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week improvement falls below 1 point after prior weeks of larger gains
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT week-on-week gain slowed from 4.0 to 0.7 points in the most recent week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues rising over the next 2 weeks despite TRANSIT's deceleration, rejecting the policy-caution mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined every week for four consecutive weeks (25.0 to 20.3), reflecting an ongoing structural shift away from staying home. This steady, always-on decline mechanically frees time for out-of-home activity and should raise RETAIL_REC within the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined every week for 4 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the next week despite RESIDENTIAL continuing its multi-week decline, rejecting the always-on relationship.
